# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

1	# u8-l8 确定性执行：deterministic_mode 从配置到内核
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 说清 `deterministic_mode` 的设计定位：它是一个 **opt-in（显式开启）的执行策略开关**，只决定「以什么方式执行计算」，与「数值兼容性」（fp16/bf16/TF32 等精度策略）完全正交；当前只支持 NVIDIA CUDA，KLXPU、ROCm 等后端开启时会直接抛 `ValueError`。
8	2. 完整追踪配置到生效的链路：`DeepSpeedConfig` 构造期 `configure_determinism` 只解析布尔开关（不改任何全局状态）→ 引擎构造最早期 `apply_determinism` 才真正应用 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 与 TF32/cuDNN 开关。
9	3. 解释 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 为什么必须在 CUDA 初始化**之前**由用户设置、DeepSpeed 为什么只「校验」而不「代设」。
10	4. 理解确定性要求如何传导到 PyTorch 检查覆盖不到的地方：Triton grouped GEMM 的 `USE_IEEE` 路径（`input_precision="ieee"` 替代 TF32 tensor core）与固定 tile 配置（绕过计时型 autotune）、legacy transformer 内核对 `stochastic_mode` 的拒绝、FPDT 对 FlashAttention backward 的传递。
11	5. 准确辨析该开关的**边界**：不改变精度、NCCL 算法、并行与重叠；不保证自定义内核与分布式调度的比特级可重复；进程全局设置销毁引擎后也不恢复。
12	
13	本讲是「高级机制」单元的一篇，依赖 u2-l2（配置系统）、u2-l3（引擎构造流程）与 u8-l3（跨拓扑迁移对可复现实验的诉求）的认知。
14	
15	## 2. 前置知识
16	
17	### 2.1 什么是「确定性执行」
18	
19	确定性（determinism）指的是：**相同的种子、相同的软硬件栈与拓扑下，两次运行产生逐位相同（bitwise identical）的结果**。它与「正确性」无关——每次结果都可能是数值上完全正确的，但两次运行之间最后几位小数不同，这就是非确定。
20	
21	深度学习训练里非确定的三个典型来源：
22	
23	1. **原子加的归约顺序**。`index_add`、`scatter_add` 以及许多 backward 内核用 `atomicAdd` 累加梯度。浮点加法不满足结合律：
24	
25	   \[ (a + b) + c \neq a + (b + c) \quad \text{（一般情形）} \]
26	
27	   而 atomicAdd 的到达顺序每次运行都可能不同，于是累加结果的舍入路径不同。
28	2. **计时型的算法选择**。cuDNN benchmark 模式（`torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True`）会实测各卷积算法后挑最快的；Triton 的 `@triton.autotune` 同样实测各 tile 配置。机器负载、时钟频率的抖动会让「最快的」每次不同，而不同算法/配置对应不同的累加分组，结果就不同。
29	3. **TF32 精度**。Ampere 及以后的 NVIDIA GPU 上，fp32 矩阵乘默认可走 TF32 tensor core：输入先舍入到 1 位符号 + 8 位指数 + 10 位显式尾数的 TF32 格式再相乘，单次乘积对输入的相对舍入误差量级为 \(2^{-11}\)，与 IEEE fp32 逐位乘不同（详见 4.2.2 节）。
30	
31	### 2.2 cuBLAS workspace 是什么
32	
33	cuBLAS（CUDA 的 BLAS 矩阵乘库）在初始化句柄时会按环境变量 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 分配工作区。PyTorch 文档规定：要让 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 对 cuBLAS 操作生效，必须在 **CUDA/cuBLAS 初始化之前** 把该变量设为 `:4096:8` 或 `:16:8`——一旦句柄已建立，workspace 尺寸就定死了，之后再改环境变量无效。这是理解 4.2 节「只校验、不代设」的关键。
34	
35	### 2.3 本讲用到的 DeepSpeed 既有机制
36	
37	- **配置两阶段设计**（u2-l2）：`DeepSpeedConfig` 构造期只做解析与校验，不碰进程全局状态；应用推迟到引擎构造期。`deterministic_mode` 是这一设计的典型样本。
38	- **引擎八阶段骨架**（u2-l3）：`DeepSpeedEngine.__init__` 从「基础属性与确定性」开始分阶段构造，`apply_determinism` 就在第一阶段。
39	- **加速器抽象层**（u3-l1）：`get_accelerator()` 返回当前后端单例；`device_name()` 是 torch 设备字符串，`_name` 是 DeepSpeed 自己的身份名——两者不一定一致（KLXPU 前者报 `"cuda"`、后者报 `"klxpu"`）。

55	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
56	
57	本讲的四个最小模块：**configure_determinism 配置解析** → **apply_determinism 引擎应用点与后端限制** → **确定性要求的内核传导（Triton IEEE 路径等）** → **确定性边界与文档声明**。
58	
59	### 4.1 configure_determinism：配置解析期什么都不改
60	
61	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
62	
63	`deterministic_mode` 是一个 **JSON 顶层布尔字段**，默认 `false`。设计上的第一原则是「解析与应用分离」：
64	
65	- `DeepSpeedConfig` 构造时只做三件事——读出布尔值、强制类型检查、挂到 `config.deterministic_mode` 属性上；
66	- 不修改用户传入的配置字典，也不碰任何进程全局 PyTorch 设置。
67	
68	为什么这么设计？因为 `DeepSpeedConfig` 的构造可能发生在「还没决定要不要真的初始化引擎」的场合（比如仅做配置校验、日志打印）。如果解析期就全局打开 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`，一个只读配置的操作会污染整个进程。教程文档明确写了这条契约：`Parsing does not change input configuration or process-global PyTorch settings.`（[docs/_tutorials/deterministic-mode.md:21](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/docs/_tutorials/deterministic-mode.md#L21)）
69	
70	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
71	
72	```text
73	DeepSpeedConfig.__init__(param_dict)
74	  ├─ 解析输入（dict / hjson 文件 / base64）
75	  ├─ _reject_removed_config_keys
76	  ├─ _initialize_params(param_dict)         # 各顶层字段
77	  ├─ _configure_train_batch_size()          # batch 三选二
78	  ├─ configure_determinism(self, param_dict)  # ← 本模块：只解析+挂属性
79	  └─ _do_sanity_check()
80	```
81	
82	注意挂载点在 `_do_sanity_check` **之前**、batch size 推导**之后**——与 u2-l2 总结的顺序一致。

84	#### 4.1.3 源码精读

129	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
130	
131	**练习 1**：为什么用 `type(enabled) is not bool` 而不是 `if not isinstance(enabled, bool)`？两者有实际差别吗？
132	
133	**答案**：对 `True/False` 两者等价。但 `type(...) is bool` 连 `bool` 的子类实例也拒绝（`isinstance` 会放行子类），是更严格的写法；实践中主要防线是拒绝 `1`/`0`（`int` 会被 `if enabled` 误判为真）与字符串。核心点：JSON 里 `true` 解析成 Python `bool`，而手写 dict 里很容易误传 `1`，这里在配置边界就拦住。
134	
135	**练习 2**：如果用户在 JSON 里同时写了 `deterministic_mode: true` 和一个不存在的顶层键，哪个先报错？
136	
137	**答案**：都不报「不存在的键」——DeepSpeed 顶层标量历史上是宽容的；真正会先触发的是 `_reject_removed_config_keys`（若命中已移除键）与 `_do_sanity_check`（在 `configure_determinism` 之后执行）。所以布尔类型错误的报错时机早于 sanity check。
138	
139	**练习 3**：`configure_determinism` 为什么不顺便检查 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`？
140	
141	**答案**：检查的语义不同。解析期检查会在「用户只想校验配置」时就因环境变量缺失而失败，且此时报告为时过早——用户可能稍后、在启动引擎前设置。环境变量校验属于「应用期前置条件」，放在 `apply_determinism` 里才能保证「检查通过的那一刻真的要应用了」。
142	
143	### 4.2 apply_determinism：引擎应用点与后端限制
144	
145	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
146	
147	`apply_determinism` 是真正改变进程全局执行策略的地方。它做四件事，顺序严格：
148	
149	1. **早退**：`deterministic_mode` 为假直接返回（任何后端、任何环境变量状态都不受影响——「关闭即 no-op」）。
150	2. **后端门卫**：只允许 NVIDIA CUDA。KLXPU（设备名报 `"cuda"` 但身份是 `"klxpu"`）和 ROCm（`torch.version.hip` 非空）都会被明确拒绝。
151	3. **环境变量前置校验**：`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 必须已经是 `:4096:8` 或 `:16:8`，否则报错。**只校验、不代设**。
152	4. **应用全局开关**：`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)`（严格模式：遇到已知非确定且无替代实现的算子直接抛异常），并关掉 TF32（matmul 与 cuDNN 两个开关）、关掉 cuDNN benchmark、打开 cuDNN deterministic。
153	
154	为什么在引擎构造的**最早期**应用？因为引擎构造的后续阶段（模型搬运到设备、优化器状态初始化、首个 forward）马上就要执行 CUDA 计算；确定性策略必须在任何一次 CUDA 矩阵乘之前就位，否则「前面的计算已经非确定了」。
155	
156	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
157	
158	```text
159	DeepSpeedEngine.__init__(...)
160	  ├─ ...基础属性...
161	  ├─ self._config = config_class
162	  ├─ if self._config.deterministic_mode:      # ← 应用点（L551-L553）
163	  │     apply_determinism(self._config)
164	  │       ├─ enabled? --否--> return（no-op）
165	  │       ├─ _is_nvidia_cuda(accelerator)? --否--> ValueError
166	  │       ├─ CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG ∈ {:4096:8, :16:8}? --否--> ValueError
167	  │       └─ torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)
168	  │          torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
169	  │          torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
170	  │          torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
171	  │          torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
172	  └─ ...后续 7 个阶段（分布式、优化器包装、检查点...）
173	```
174	
175	关于 TF32 的数值含义：TF32 把 fp32 输入舍入到 10 位显式尾数后再进 tensor core。对输入 \(x\) 的相对舍入误差为
176	
177	\[ |x - \mathrm{tf32}(x)| \le 2^{-11} \cdot |x| \]
178	
179	（尾数 10 位，ulp 为 \(2^{-10}\)，最近舍入误差不超过半个 ulp）。所以 TF32 乘积 \(a \cdot b\) 与 IEEE fp32 乘积逐位不同；确定性与「回到 IEEE fp32 乘」在这里是同一件事：`allow_tf32 = False`。

246	### 4.3 确定性要求的内核传导：Triton IEEE 路径与 stochastic_mode 拒绝
247	
248	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
249	
250	`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 只能管住 **PyTorch 原生算子**。DeepSpeed 有一批自己的内核，PyTorch 的检查鞭长莫及，确定性要求必须由各内核**自行查询并响应**。目前的传导点有三处：
251	
252	1. **Triton grouped GEMM（正向传导）**：两个非确定来源都处理了——(a) `@triton.autotune` 是计时型选择，绕过之；(b) `tl.dot` 对 fp32 输入默认用 TF32 tensor core，而 `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False` **管不到 Triton**，所以显式传 `input_precision="ieee"`。
253	2. **legacy `DeepSpeedTransformerLayer`（反向拒绝）**：其 `stochastic_mode=True` 的高性能 CUDA 内核本身就是随机化的，与确定性互斥，直接抛 `RuntimeError`。
254	3. **FPDT（参数传递）**：把 PyTorch 确定性标志原样传给 FlashAttention backward 的 `deterministic` 形参，由 flash-attn 内核选择确定性的 dq/dk/dv 累加实现。
255	
256	顺带说明：`deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/swiglu_triton.py` 既不含 `tl.dot`（无 TF32 问题）也不含计时型 autotune，是逐元素内核，因此不在确定性关键路径上、无需特殊处理。

258	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
259	
260	grouped GEMM 的确定性选择发生在每次 kernel launch 的公共入口：
261	
262	```text
263	_launch_group_gemm(kernel, configs, grid, ...)
264	  ├─ deterministic = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()   # 查询全局开关
265	  ├─ kwargs["USE_IEEE"] = deterministic                             # 精度位传入内核
266	  └─ if deterministic:
267	        config = configs[0]          # 固定取第一个配置
268	        kernel.fn[grid](..., **config.kwargs, num_warps=..., num_stages=...)  # 绕过 autotune
269	     else:
270	        kernel[grid](...)            # 正常走 @triton.autotune（计时选择）
271	```
272	
273	内核内部（前向与权重梯度两个内核同构）：
274	
275	```text
276	if USE_IEEE:                                    # tl.constexpr，编译期特化
277	    acc += tl.dot(a_tile, b_tile, input_precision="ieee")   # IEEE fp32 乘加
278	else:
279	    acc += tl.dot(a_tile, b_tile)               # fp32 默认走 TF32 tensor core
280	```
281	
282	为什么 autotune 非确定：`@triton.autotune(configs=..., key=[...])` 会在每个新 key（此处是 `KC/NO/NUM_GROUPS` 等形状参数）首次出现时实测全部 6 个候选配置并缓存最优者。实测耗时受机器瞬时负载影响，两次运行可能选中不同的 `BLOCK_K`，而 `BLOCK_K` 决定 K 维归约的分组方式——`acc += tl.dot(...)` 的累加分组变了，舍入路径就变了。

340	### 4.4 确定性边界：能保证什么、不能保证什么
341	
342	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
343	
344	这是本讲最重要、也最容易被误解的模块。`deterministic_mode` 的契约边界（全部来自官方文档声明）：
345	
346	**它能保证/做到的**：
347	
348	1. PyTorch 原生算子走确定性实现；已知非确定且无替代的算子在严格模式下直接抛异常。
349	2. TF32（cuBLAS matmul、cuDNN、Triton grouped GEMM 三处）被关闭，回到 IEEE fp32 乘。
350	3. cuDNN benchmark 关闭、deterministic 打开——算法选择不再依赖计时。
351	4. Triton grouped GEMM 的 tile 配置固定、FPDT 传确定性标志、stochastic_mode 组合被拒绝。
352	
353	**它不保证/不做的**：
354	
355	1. **不改变数值精度策略**：不改变梯度精度、GAS、TP/EP、overlap、NCCL 算法、AutoEP 算术——「开确定性」不等于「换 Megatron 数值方案」。
356	2. **不覆盖自定义内核与分布式调度**：PyTorch 的检查管不到 DeepSpeed/用户自定义 CUDA 内核与集合通信的调度；配置被接受 ≠ 负载比特级可复现，需要在固定软硬件栈与拓扑上独立验证整个负载。
357	3. **不追认历史**：引擎初始化不能让更早的模型构建或 CUDA 操作变确定；种子、数据顺序、checkpoint 的 RNG/dataloader 状态都由调用方负责。
358	4. **进程全局且不可逆**：设置在引擎销毁或后续创建禁用引擎时**不恢复**——它是进程级策略，不是引擎级作用域。
359	5. 不提供 Megatron 比特级兼容承诺；不因「配置没测过」而拒绝配置（现有校验照常执行）。
360	
361	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
362	
363	官方契约测试如何验证「跨进程逐位可复现」：
364	
365	```text
366	test_independent_cuda_training(stage ∈ {0, 2, 3})
367	  for repeat in 0..1:
368	      subprocess: torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 本测试文件
369	                  env: CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=":4096:8", OMP_NUM_THREADS="1"
370	      worker(): 种子 1234 → Linear-Tanh-Linear + AdamW
371	                → deepspeed.initialize(deterministic_mode=True, zero stage)
372	                → 断言 5 个全局开关已就位
373	                → 6 个 microstep，边界处快照 output/grad/master/exp_avg/exp_avg_sq
374	                → torch.save(snapshots)
375	  assert_equal(两次快照)   # uint8 视图逐位比较

# u8-l8 确定性执行：deterministic_mode 从配置到内核

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清 `deterministic_mode` 的设计定位：它是一个 **opt-in（显式开启）的执行策略开关**，只决定「以什么方式执行计算」，与「数值兼容性」（fp16/bf16/TF32 等精度策略）完全正交；当前只支持 NVIDIA CUDA，KLXPU、ROCm 等后端开启时会直接抛 `ValueError`。
2. 完整追踪配置到生效的链路：`DeepSpeedConfig` 构造期 `configure_determinism` 只解析布尔开关（不改任何全局状态）→ 引擎构造最早期 `apply_determinism` 才真正应用 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 与 TF32/cuDNN 开关。
3. 解释 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 为什么必须在 CUDA 初始化**之前**由用户设置、DeepSpeed 为什么只「校验」而不「代设」。
4. 理解确定性要求如何传导到 PyTorch 检查覆盖不到的地方：Triton grouped GEMM 的 `USE_IEEE` 路径（`input_precision="ieee"` 替代 TF32 tensor core）与固定 tile 配置（绕过计时型 autotune）、legacy transformer 内核对 `stochastic_mode` 的拒绝、FPDT 对 FlashAttention backward 的传递。
5. 准确辨析该开关的**边界**：不改变精度、NCCL 算法、并行与重叠；不保证自定义内核与分布式调度的比特级可重复；进程全局设置销毁引擎后也不恢复。

本讲是「高级机制」单元的一篇，依赖 u2-l2（配置系统）、u2-l3（引擎构造流程）与 u8-l3（跨拓扑迁移对可复现实验的诉求）的认知。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 什么是「确定性执行」

确定性（determinism）指的是：**相同的种子、相同的软硬件栈与拓扑下，两次运行产生逐位相同（bitwise identical）的结果**。它与「正确性」无关——每次结果都可能是数值上完全正确的，但两次运行之间最后几位小数不同，这就是非确定。

深度学习训练里非确定的三个典型来源：

1. **原子加的归约顺序**。`index_add`、`scatter_add` 以及许多 backward 内核用 `atomicAdd` 累加梯度。浮点加法不满足结合律：

   \[ (a + b) + c \neq a + (b + c) \quad \text{（一般情形）} \]

   而 atomicAdd 的到达顺序每次运行都可能不同，于是累加结果的舍入路径不同。
2. **计时型的算法选择**。cuDNN benchmark 模式（`torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True`）会实测各卷积算法后挑最快的；Triton 的 `@triton.autotune` 同样实测各 tile 配置。机器负载、时钟频率的抖动会让「最快的」每次不同，而不同算法/配置对应不同的累加分组，结果就不同。
3. **TF32 精度**。Ampere 及以后的 NVIDIA GPU 上，fp32 矩阵乘默认可走 TF32 tensor core：输入先舍入到 1 位符号 + 8 位指数 + 10 位显式尾数的 TF32 格式再相乘，单次乘积对输入的相对舍入误差量级为 \(2^{-11}\)，与 IEEE fp32 逐位乘不同（详见 4.2.2 节）。

### 2.2 cuBLAS workspace 是什么

cuBLAS（CUDA 的 BLAS 矩阵乘库）在初始化句柄时会按环境变量 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 分配工作区。PyTorch 文档规定：要让 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 对 cuBLAS 操作生效，必须在 **CUDA/cuBLAS 初始化之前** 把该变量设为 `:4096:8` 或 `:16:8`——一旦句柄已建立，workspace 尺寸就定死了，之后再改环境变量无效。这是理解 4.2 节「只校验、不代设」的关键。

### 2.3 本讲用到的 DeepSpeed 既有机制

- **配置两阶段设计**（u2-l2）：`DeepSpeedConfig` 构造期只做解析与校验，不碰进程全局状态；应用推迟到引擎构造期。`deterministic_mode` 是这一设计的典型样本。
- **引擎八阶段骨架**（u2-l3）：`DeepSpeedEngine.__init__` 从「基础属性与确定性」开始分阶段构造，`apply_determinism` 就在第一阶段。
- **加速器抽象层**（u3-l1）：`get_accelerator()` 返回当前后端单例；`device_name()` 是 torch 设备字符串，`_name` 是 DeepSpeed 自己的身份名——两者不一定一致（KLXPU 前者报 `"cuda"`、后者报 `"klxpu"`）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲的四个最小模块：**configure_determinism 配置解析** → **apply_determinism 引擎应用点与后端限制** → **确定性要求的内核传导（Triton IEEE 路径等）** → **确定性边界与文档声明**。

### 4.1 configure_determinism：配置解析期什么都不改

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`deterministic_mode` 是一个 **JSON 顶层布尔字段**，默认 `false`。设计上的第一原则是「解析与应用分离」：

- `DeepSpeedConfig` 构造时只做三件事——读出布尔值、强制类型检查、挂到 `config.deterministic_mode` 属性上；
- 不修改用户传入的配置字典，也不碰任何进程全局 PyTorch 设置。

为什么这么设计？因为 `DeepSpeedConfig` 的构造可能发生在「还没决定要不要真的初始化引擎」的场合（比如仅做配置校验、日志打印）。如果解析期就全局打开 `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`，一个只读配置的操作会污染整个进程。教程文档明确写了这条契约：`Parsing does not change input configuration or process-global PyTorch settings.`（[docs/_tutorials/deterministic-mode.md:21](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/docs/_tutorials/deterministic-mode.md#L21)）

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
DeepSpeedConfig.__init__(param_dict)
  ├─ 解析输入（dict / hjson 文件 / base64）
  ├─ _reject_removed_config_keys
  ├─ _initialize_params(param_dict)         # 各顶层字段
  ├─ _configure_train_batch_size()          # batch 三选二
  ├─ configure_determinism(self, param_dict)  # ← 本模块：只解析+挂属性
  └─ _do_sanity_check()
```

注意挂载点在 `_do_sanity_check` **之前**、batch size 推导**之后**——与 u2-l2 总结的顺序一致。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

解析函数本体只有 5 行：

[deepspeed/runtime/determinism.py:10-14](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/deepspeed/runtime/determinism.py#L10-L14) —— `configure_determinism` 从 `param_dict` 读取 `deterministic_mode`（缺省 `False`）；用 `type(enabled) is not bool` 严格校验必须是 JSON 布尔（写 `1`、`0`、`"true"` 都会抛 `ValueError`，这比 `if not enabled` 严格——`1` 会被误当 `True`）；最后只做一件事：把结果写到 `config.deterministic_mode` 属性。

调用挂载点：

[deepspeed/runtime/config.py:478-484](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/deepspeed/runtime/config.py#L478-L484) —— `DeepSpeedConfig.__init__` 先 `copy.copy(self._param_dict)` 传副本（注释说明是为了不修改用户 json，例如用于日志），随后依次 `_initialize_params` → `_configure_train_batch_size` → `configure_determinism(self, param_dict)` → `_do_sanity_check()`。确定性解析被插在 batch size 推导之后、一致性检查之前。

配套的 no-op 测试证明「关闭时完全无副作用」：

[tests/unit/runtime/test_determinism.py:64-68](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/tests/unit/runtime/test_determinism.py#L64-L68) —— `test_disabled_runtime_is_noop` 先删掉 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 环境变量，记录 `torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()` 的当前值，构造一个不带 `deterministic_mode` 的配置并调用 `apply_determinism`，断言全局开关前后不变。这个测试同时覆盖了「解析」与「应用」两层的 no-op 语义。

预期结果：解析只挂属性、不改全局；类型校验严格。本实践可在纯 CPU 环境（无任何 GPU）执行。待本地验证。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么用 `type(enabled) is not bool` 而不是 `if not isinstance(enabled, bool)`？两者有实际差别吗？

**答案**：对 `True/False` 两者等价。但 `type(...) is bool` 连 `bool` 的子类实例也拒绝（`isinstance` 会放行子类），是更严格的写法；实践中主要防线是拒绝 `1`/`0`（`int` 会被 `if enabled` 误判为真）与字符串。核心点：JSON 里 `true` 解析成 Python `bool`，而手写 dict 里很容易误传 `1`，这里在配置边界就拦住。

**练习 2**：如果用户在 JSON 里同时写了 `deterministic_mode: true` 和一个不存在的顶层键，哪个先报错？

**答案**：都不报「不存在的键」——DeepSpeed 顶层标量历史上是宽容的；真正会先触发的是 `_reject_removed_config_keys`（若命中已移除键）与 `_do_sanity_check`（在 `configure_determinism` 之后执行）。所以布尔类型错误的报错时机早于 sanity check。

**练习 3**：`configure_determinism` 为什么不顺便检查 `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`？

**答案**：检查的语义不同。解析期检查会在「用户只想校验配置」时就因环境变量缺失而失败，且此时报告为时过早——用户可能稍后、在启动引擎前设置。环境变量校验属于「应用期前置条件」，放在 `apply_determinism` 里才能保证「检查通过的那一刻真的要应用了」。

### 4.2 apply_determinism：引擎应用点与后端限制

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`apply_determinism` 是真正改变进程全局执行策略的地方。它做四件事，顺序严格：

1. **早退**：`deterministic_mode` 为假直接返回（任何后端、任何环境变量状态都不受影响——「关闭即 no-op」）。
2. **后端门卫**：只允许 NVIDIA CUDA。KLXPU（设备名报 `"cuda"` 但身份是 `"klxpu"`）和 ROCm（`torch.version.hip` 非空）都会被明确拒绝。
3. **环境变量前置校验**：`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` 必须已经是 `:4096:8` 或 `:16:8`，否则报错。**只校验、不代设**。
4. **应用全局开关**：`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)`（严格模式：遇到已知非确定且无替代实现的算子直接抛异常），并关掉 TF32（matmul 与 cuDNN 两个开关）、关掉 cuDNN benchmark、打开 cuDNN deterministic。

为什么在引擎构造的**最早期**应用？因为引擎构造的后续阶段（模型搬运到设备、优化器状态初始化、首个 forward）马上就要执行 CUDA 计算；确定性策略必须在任何一次 CUDA 矩阵乘之前就位，否则「前面的计算已经非确定了」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
DeepSpeedEngine.__init__(...)
  ├─ ...基础属性...
  ├─ self._config = config_class
  ├─ if self._config.deterministic_mode:      # ← 应用点（L551-L553）
  │     apply_determinism(self._config)
  │       ├─ enabled? --否--> return（no-op）
  │       ├─ _is_nvidia_cuda(accelerator)? --否--> ValueError
  │       ├─ CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG ∈ {:4096:8, :16:8}? --否--> ValueError
  │       └─ torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)
  │          torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
  │          torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
  │          torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
  │          torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
  └─ ...后续 7 个阶段（分布式、优化器包装、检查点...）
```

关于 TF32 的数值含义：TF32 把 fp32 输入舍入到 10 位显式尾数后再进 tensor core。对输入 \(x\) 的相对舍入误差为

\[ |x - \mathrm{tf32}(x)| \le 2^{-11} \cdot |x| \]

（尾数 10 位，ulp 为 \(2^{-10}\)，最近舍入误差不超过半个 ulp）。所以 TF32 乘积 \(a \cdot b\) 与 IEEE fp32 乘积逐位不同；确定性与「回到 IEEE fp32 乘」在这里是同一件事：`allow_tf32 = False`。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `apply_determinism` 不自己 `os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"` 帮用户设好？

**答案**：环境变量只在 cuBLAS 句柄创建时读取一次。到引擎构造时，进程里很可能已经跑过 CUDA 操作（模型构建、`deepspeed.initialize` 之前的用户代码），workspace 已经按旧配置分配完；此时代设环境变量毫无效果，却会让用户误以为确定性已生效——静默假阳性比显式报错危险得多。所以 DeepSpeed 选择「校验而非安装」，并把失败信息写清楚（教程原句：`Workspace settings are validated, not installed too late.`）。

**练习 2**：`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=False)` 里 `warn_only=False` 意味着什么？改成 `True` 会怎样？

**答案**：`warn_only=False`（严格模式）下，PyTorch 遇到已知非确定且无确定性替代实现的算子（如某些 `index_add` CUDA 路径）直接抛 `RuntimeError`；`warn_only=True` 则只发警告继续跑。DeepSpeed 选严格模式，理由是「半确定的确定性模式」会误导调试。教程还注明：即便是 warn-only 模式（用户自己改的），Triton grouped GEMM 的确定性路径依然会被选中，因为它们查的是 `are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()` 而非 warn_only 标志。

**练习 3**：一个用户在 KLXPU 集群上设置 `deterministic_mode: true` 训练，报错信息是什么？如果他想「先跑通再说」该怎么办？

**答案**：`ValueError: deterministic_mode currently supports NVIDIA CUDA only`。正确做法是把配置里的 `deterministic_mode` 去掉或设为 `false`——文档明确「disabled 行为完全不变（no-op）」，而不是去伪造环境变量或加速器身份。

### 4.3 确定性要求的内核传导：Triton IEEE 路径与 stochastic_mode 拒绝

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` 只能管住 **PyTorch 原生算子**。DeepSpeed 有一批自己的内核，PyTorch 的检查鞭长莫及，确定性要求必须由各内核**自行查询并响应**。目前的传导点有三处：

1. **Triton grouped GEMM（正向传导）**：两个非确定来源都处理了——(a) `@triton.autotune` 是计时型选择，绕过之；(b) `tl.dot` 对 fp32 输入默认用 TF32 tensor core，而 `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False` **管不到 Triton**，所以显式传 `input_precision="ieee"`。
2. **legacy `DeepSpeedTransformerLayer`（反向拒绝）**：其 `stochastic_mode=True` 的高性能 CUDA 内核本身就是随机化的，与确定性互斥，直接抛 `RuntimeError`。
3. **FPDT（参数传递）**：把 PyTorch 确定性标志原样传给 FlashAttention backward 的 `deterministic` 形参，由 flash-attn 内核选择确定性的 dq/dk/dv 累加实现。

顺带说明：`deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/swiglu_triton.py` 既不含 `tl.dot`（无 TF32 问题）也不含计时型 autotune，是逐元素内核，因此不在确定性关键路径上、无需特殊处理。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

grouped GEMM 的确定性选择发生在每次 kernel launch 的公共入口：

```text
_launch_group_gemm(kernel, configs, grid, ...)
  ├─ deterministic = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()   # 查询全局开关
  ├─ kwargs["USE_IEEE"] = deterministic                             # 精度位传入内核
  └─ if deterministic:
        config = configs[0]          # 固定取第一个配置
        kernel.fn[grid](..., **config.kwargs, num_warps=..., num_stages=...)  # 绕过 autotune
     else:
        kernel[grid](...)            # 正常走 @triton.autotune（计时选择）
```

内核内部（前向与权重梯度两个内核同构）：

```text
if USE_IEEE:                                    # tl.constexpr，编译期特化
    acc += tl.dot(a_tile, b_tile, input_precision="ieee")   # IEEE fp32 乘加
else:
    acc += tl.dot(a_tile, b_tile)               # fp32 默认走 TF32 tensor core
```

为什么 autotune 非确定：`@triton.autotune(configs=..., key=[...])` 会在每个新 key（此处是 `KC/NO/NUM_GROUPS` 等形状参数）首次出现时实测全部 6 个候选配置并缓存最优者。实测耗时受机器瞬时负载影响，两次运行可能选中不同的 `BLOCK_K`，而 `BLOCK_K` 决定 K 维归约的分组方式——`acc += tl.dot(...)` 的累加分组变了，舍入路径就变了。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False` 已经关了 TF32，为什么 Triton 内核还要单独的 `input_precision="ieee"`？

**答案**：PyTorch 的 TF32 开关只作用于 PyTorch 调用的 cuBLAS/cuDNN 矩阵乘。Triton 内核里的 `tl.dot` 由 Triton 编译器直接生成 tensor core 指令，fp32 输入下默认仍用 TF32 精度，完全不经过 PyTorch 的后端开关。所以必须用 Triton 自己的 `input_precision="ieee"` 参数显式覆盖——这正是教程那句 `disabling PyTorch TF32 does not control Triton input precision` 的含义。

**练习 2**：固定 `configs[0]` 而不是「跑一次计时后锁定最优」有什么取舍？

**答案**：跑一次计时再锁定，结果仍依赖当次机器状态，跨进程/跨节点不可复现（每个进程都要重新计时，不同节点可能锁定不同配置）；固定 `configs[0]` 是纯函数式的确定选择，任何机器任何时刻都一样，代价是可能不是该形状的最优 tile——用性能换可复现，且教程已声明 `may reduce performance`。

**练习 3**：为什么 legacy transformer 选「拒绝」而不是「自动关闭 stochastic_mode 继续跑」？

**答案**：`stochastic_mode=True` 是用户显式要的高性能随机化执行，静默改写用户意图（自动降级）会让性能与行为都偏离预期。确定性模式下「拒绝并报错」把选择权交还用户：要么关 `stochastic_mode`，要么关确定性。教程原句：`legacy stochastic execution raises rather than silently proceeding`。

### 4.4 确定性边界：能保证什么、不能保证什么

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

这是本讲最重要、也最容易被误解的模块。`deterministic_mode` 的契约边界（全部来自官方文档声明）：

**它能保证/做到的**：

1. PyTorch 原生算子走确定性实现；已知非确定且无替代的算子在严格模式下直接抛异常。
2. TF32（cuBLAS matmul、cuDNN、Triton grouped GEMM 三处）被关闭，回到 IEEE fp32 乘。
3. cuDNN benchmark 关闭、deterministic 打开——算法选择不再依赖计时。
4. Triton grouped GEMM 的 tile 配置固定、FPDT 传确定性标志、stochastic_mode 组合被拒绝。

**它不保证/不做的**：

1. **不改变数值精度策略**：不改变梯度精度、GAS、TP/EP、overlap、NCCL 算法、AutoEP 算术——「开确定性」不等于「换 Megatron 数值方案」。
2. **不覆盖自定义内核与分布式调度**：PyTorch 的检查管不到 DeepSpeed/用户自定义 CUDA 内核与集合通信的调度；配置被接受 ≠ 负载比特级可复现，需要在固定软硬件栈与拓扑上独立验证整个负载。
3. **不追认历史**：引擎初始化不能让更早的模型构建或 CUDA 操作变确定；种子、数据顺序、checkpoint 的 RNG/dataloader 状态都由调用方负责。
4. **进程全局且不可逆**：设置在引擎销毁或后续创建禁用引擎时**不恢复**——它是进程级策略，不是引擎级作用域。
5. 不提供 Megatron 比特级兼容承诺；不因「配置没测过」而拒绝配置（现有校验照常执行）。

```python
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys

import torch


def weight_digest(model):
    sha = hashlib.sha256()
    for p in model.parameters():
        sha.update(p.detach().cpu().contiguous().reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).numpy().tobytes())
    return sha.hexdigest()


def main():
    import deepspeed
    torch.manual_seed(1234)
    model = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(8, 16), torch.nn.Tanh(), torch.nn.Linear(16, 4))
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    engine, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(
        model=model, optimizer=optimizer,
        config={"train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 2,
                "gradient_accumulation_steps": 2,
                "deterministic_mode": True,
                "zero_allow_untested_optimizer": True,
                "zero_optimization": {"stage": int(sys.argv[1]), "overlap_comm": False}})
    losses = []
    for microstep in range(6):
        out = engine(torch.randn(2, 8, device=engine.device))
        loss = out.square().mean()
        engine.backward(loss)
        boundary = engine.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary()
        engine.step()
        if boundary:
            losses.append(loss.item())
    print(json.dumps({"losses": losses, "digest": weight_digest(engine.module)}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**答案**：按契约逐项排查：(a) 种子与数据顺序是否两次一致（调用方责任）；(b) 是否有 checkpoint 恢复且 RNG/dataloader 状态没保存（调用方责任）；(c) `deterministic_mode` 是否在**任何 CUDA 操作之前**生效（模型构建早于引擎初始化的部分不受保护）；(d) 是否使用了自定义内核/算子（PyTorch 检查不覆盖）；(e) 分布式调度（NCCL 算法、overlap 顺序）是否两次不同——文档明确不保证这部分；(f) 两次软硬件栈是否完全一致（驱动、torch、GPU 型号）。

- `deterministic_mode` 是 opt-in 的**执行策略**开关，与数值精度策略正交；默认 false 且关闭即完全 no-op；当前仅支持 NVIDIA CUDA，KLXPU（设备名 cuda、身份 klxpu）与 ROCm（hip 非空）都会被 `_is_nvidia_cuda` 的三重条件拒绝。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
